hypothesis: A previously unknown one-bit latent regime makes identical visible state/action pairs have different public consequences. Standard WSP80 Markov source-blind editor is misspecified. Can a paid-history-conditioned weight compiler infer a compact latent transition mechanism and predict held-out public outcomes without private regime labels?

source.role: new independent evaluator-only history-dependent source module; not WSP80 source.py
source.public_states: all 64 six-bit states; six actions; latent state is unobservable to learner
source.hidden_rules: All worlds start latent z=0, visible before state all zeros. Every action a flips visible bit a. For hidden_two_mode: an unknown trigger action t changes the latent z AFTER the visible transition. When pre-action z=1 and a!=t, an additional bit (a+offset)%6 is flipped (offset in [1..5]). Trigger and offset derive from SHA256('WSP81|DEV|seed|private-params-v1') and are invisible to learner. memoryless_control has no hidden flip (only visible action-bit toggle). Source no reset during paid session.
source.observables: Only before state, public action, after state, one-unit charge, ordered action history. No latent labels/unknown trigger/offset/physics oracle in any learner or action selector.
source.schedule: 384 physically paid steps per world. StageA 144 actions use SHA256('WSP81|DEV|seed|stageA|step') modulo 6. StageB 240 actions use SHA256('WSP81|DEV|seed|stageB|step') modulo 6. Entire action schedule fixed without source/private knowledge; no reset, no free queries.
source.private_evaluation: For each context, evaluator assigns appropriate latent z after applying context from initial z=0, then scores ALL 384 public state/action queries with private source transition. Exactly 768 queries per world; 4608 total. Counterfactual public-state conditioning is a fixed evaluator query and may contain states unreachable from context; it is not paid training data.

models.new_history_aware_numeric: Learn from charged trajectory by enumerating 31 predefined hypotheses: one memoryless XOR-action baseline plus t in 0..5 and offset in 1..5 for the two-state family. Reject inconsistent hypotheses using ONLY ordered charged public observations. Convert all surviving hypotheses to numeric ReLU readout for public visible transition and a history-conditioned numeric binary mode register. Cold inference uses frozen numeric weights/mode triggers; abstains if surviving hypotheses disagree. Class discovery is NOT open-ended.
models.independent_symbolic_same_family: Separate implementation from charged trajectory only, same 31 hypothesis class, same abstention rule. Exact parity is required, so a tie is NOT an intelligence advantage.
models.legacy_markov: WSP80 PaidStructuralWeightEditor trained sequentially on exactly same 384 charged public rows; record if it refuses conflicting deterministic duplicates. Never alter WSP80 source.
models.memoryless_control: Fixed visible XOR-action baseline, ignores history; same 768 private queries.
models.paid_lookup: Only public (visible state, action) pairs from charged ledger, abstain on contradictions/unseen pairs. No regime labels or private truth.
models.conventional: Existing full WSP77 Adam 12->32->6 baseline trained from 384 public rows with 3 fixed restarts, 6000 maximum updates each, confidence and convergence receipts. This is memoryless and cannot substitute for strong history-aware symbolic control.

stop_criteria: Use exactly the six frozen seeds and the single 384-action trajectory each. Preserve all negative results. If training cannot fit, report negative/UNVERIFIED; do not change source, allocation, seed, family or thresholds in this protocol.
interpretation: This is genuinely out of WSP80's deterministic visible-state Markov assumption, but the new learner receives a PREDEFINED finite latent-family hypothesis class. It cannot prove discovery of an unforeseen law, general intelligence, broad transfer, language ability, or superiority over same-expressivity symbolic inference.
